<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  document.body.classList.add("papers-page");

  function getCellValue(row, index) {
    return row.children[index] ? row.children[index].innerText.trim() : "";
  }

  function compareRows(a, b, index, asNumber) {
    const valA = getCellValue(a, index);
    const valB = getCellValue(b, index);
    if (asNumber) {
      return (parseFloat(valA) || 0) - (parseFloat(valB) || 0);
    }
    return valA.localeCompare(valB, undefined, { numeric: true, sensitivity: "base" });
  }

  function sortTable(table, columnIndex, direction, asNumber) {
    const tbody = table.tBodies[0];
    if (!tbody) return;
    const rows = Array.from(tbody.rows);
    rows.sort((a, b) => {
      const result = compareRows(a, b, columnIndex, asNumber);
      return direction === "desc" ? -result : result;
    });
    rows.forEach((row) => tbody.appendChild(row));
  }

  // Every table auto-sorts by Year (newest first); click any header to re-sort by that column.
  document.querySelectorAll("main.content table").forEach((table) => {
    const headerRow = table.tHead && table.tHead.rows[0];
    if (!headerRow) return;

    let yearIndex = -1;
    Array.from(headerRow.cells).forEach((cell, index) => {
      cell.dataset.sortDir = "";
      if (cell.innerText.trim().toLowerCase() === "year") {
        yearIndex = index;
      }
      cell.addEventListener("click", () => {
        const isNumber = cell.innerText.trim().toLowerCase() === "year";
        const nextDir = cell.dataset.sortDir === "desc" ? "asc" : "desc";
        Array.from(headerRow.cells).forEach((c) => (c.dataset.sortDir = ""));
        cell.dataset.sortDir = nextDir;
        sortTable(table, index, nextDir, isNumber);
      });
    });

    if (yearIndex !== -1) {
      sortTable(table, yearIndex, "desc", true);
      headerRow.cells[yearIndex].dataset.sortDir = "desc";
    }
  });
});
</script>

This is my structured collection of papers relevant to my PhD research and associated projects.

The categories provide a high-level view of the research landscape. The Key Finding column captures the main takeaway for each paper so comparisons across the literature.

---

## PhD Papers

### 1. Open-Ended Learning

Papers focused on agents that autonomously discover goals, explore unfamiliar environments, acquire skills, and adapt over time. This section is separate from self-evolution: the focus is on continuing to learn from interaction, not rewriting or evolving the agent itself.

| Paper | Year | Research Focus | What Changes | Key Finding | Source |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| A Motivational Architecture for Open-Ended Learning Challenges in Robots | 2025 | Open-ended robotic learning | Goals, skills, and adaptation | H-GRAIL combines intrinsic motivations and learning mechanisms to discover goals, acquire skills, sequence them, and adapt to changing environments. | [Link](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.18454) |
| Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models | 2023 | Open-ended embodied agents | Skill library and exploration | Voyager builds a reusable skill library through lifelong exploration, enabling strong Minecraft exploration, tech-tree progress, and zero-shot generalisation. | [Link](https://voyager.minedojo.org/) |
| Look Before You Leap: Autonomous Exploration for LLM Agents | 2026 | Autonomous exploration | Exploration before task execution | Separating environment exploration from task execution helps agents acquire grounded knowledge and generalise better in unfamiliar environments. | [Link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16143) |

---

### 2. Self-Evolution & Self-Improvement

Papers exploring systems that improve, evolve, or modify their own policies, code, or problem-solving methods beyond a fixed training procedure.

| Paper | Year | Research Focus | What Changes | Key Finding | Source |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Recursive Multi-Agent Systems | 2026 | Latent-space recursive multi-agent | Inter-agent communication / latent states | Latent communication can improve multi-agent reasoning while reducing inference cost and token use | [Link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25917/) |
| **Darwin Gödel Machine** | 2025 | Self-improving agents | Agent code / system |An archive of diverse agent lineages helps avoid local optima and enables later improvements from earlier discoveries. | [Link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.22954) |
| AlphaEvolve | 2025 | Automated algorithm discovery | Programs / algorithms | Evolutionary search over programs discovers new algorithms that outperform prior human-designed solutions. | [Link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13131) |
| **Evolver: Self-Evolving LLM Agents through Experience** | 2025 | Self-evolving agents via experience | Agent policy / behaviour | Agents can distill experience into reusable strategies and use them to improve future behaviour. | [Link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.16079) |
| A Self-Improving Coding Agent | 2025 | Self-improving coding agents | Coding agent | An agent can iteratively rewrite and improve its own coding capabilities without external supervision. | [Link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15228) |

---

### 3. Multi-Agent Systems & Collective Reasoning

Papers exploring how multiple agents communicate, debate, coordinate, specialise, or collectively solve problems.

| Paper | Year | Research Focus | What Changes | Key Finding | Source |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Improving Multi-Agent Debate with Sparse Communication Topology | 2024 | Effect of communication topology on debate | Communication topology | Sparse communication topologies can match or exceed fully-connected debate while reducing communication cost. | [Link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11776) |
| Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate | 2023 | Improving factual accuracy via debate | Reasoning / decision | Multiple language model agents debating and critiquing each other's answers improves factual accuracy and reasoning quality. | [Link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14325) |
| ReConcile: Round-Table Conference Improves Reasoning via Consensus among Diverse LLMs | 2023 | Reaching consensus among diverse LLMs | Final decision | Structured rounds of discussion between diverse LLMs help them converge on more accurate shared answers. | [Link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.13007) |

---

### 4. Agentic Learning, Tools & Interaction

Papers exploring agents that learn through interaction, tool use, tasks, feedback, or increasingly autonomous workflows.

| Paper | Year | Research Focus | What Changes | Key Finding | Source |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| AutoResearchBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Complex Scientific Literature Discovery | 2026 | Benchmarking scientific literature discovery | Agent capability | Current agents still struggle with complex, multi-step scientific literature discovery tasks. | [Link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25256) |
| MUA-RL: Multi-turn User-interacting Agent Reinforcement Learning for Agentic Tool Use | 2025 | Training agents for multi-turn tool use | Agent policy / tool use | Reinforcement learning over multi-turn user interactions improves an agent's ability to use tools effectively. | [Link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18669) |
| SoK: Agentic Skills — Beyond Tool Use in LLM Agents | 2026 | Reusable agentic skills | Procedural capabilities and skill lifecycle | Agentic skills are reusable modules beyond atomic tool calls; the paper maps their discovery, storage, composition, evaluation, and update. | [Link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20867) |
